mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next 5 trading days, investors anticipate future rate hikes, which reduces the present value of equity cash flows, producing a negative S&P 500 forward return over the following 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified trigger window (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed the trigger threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in CPIAUCSL of at least 0.3% for two consecutive months signals disinflation, prompting a shift from rate hikes to rate cuts expectations, which tends to lift equity valuations and drive positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥0.3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive during the trigger period (t-test p ≥ 0.05), or CPIAUCSL does not meet the two-month decline threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) of at least 100,000 jobs in a single month coincides with strong hiring momentum, which raises economic confidence and supports a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥100,000 in one month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during the trigger window (IC ≥ 0.05), or PAYEMS does not meet the job addition threshold.

mechanism_narrative: When both HOUST (industrial production) and RSAFS (retail sales) show double-digit month-over-month growth in the same month, it signals robust demand across sectors, which tends to precede a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase by ≥10% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive during the joint growth trigger (t-test p ≥ 0.05), or either HOUST or RSAFS does not meet the growth threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production index) of more than 5% in a month indicates supply-side weakness, which reduces future earnings expectations and tends to produce negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not consistently negative during INDPRO contraction periods (IC < 0.1 over rolling windows), or INDPRO recovers without a sustained contraction.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months, it suggests labor market softening and reduced wage growth expectations, which often precedes a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during the UNRATE cooling regime (t-test p ≥ 0.05), or UNRATE does not sustain the threshold for three months.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent FEDFUNDS declines below 2%, the discount rate is effectively lowered, increasing the present value of future equity cash flows and typically generating positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-positive over multiple consecutive rate-cutting months (IC ≥ 0.15), or FEDFUNDS does not fall below 2% as predicted.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both GDPC1 (GDP) and HOUST (industrial production) by at least 2% in a month signal demand weakness, which can depress corporate earnings expectations and drive negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decrease by ≥2% in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during the identified contraction (t-test p ≥ 0.05), or either GDPC1 or HOUST does not meet the decline threshold.
